1631844682727673856.a: Thanks to a friend out here there is a #Nabu #RetroComputing system headed my way. Missing keyboard. I used to do reverse engineering in my youth kinda like some people did crosswords. Trying to rehab my brain with something old familiar. Plan is to build Nabu Bluetooth keyboard.

1631929295185534976.a:
@voyles_jason Keyboard talks over a serial port. I believe it is RS-422 like the rest of the ports. Kinda like a Mac but weird and CP/Mish. DJ Sures has a video where he breaks down the Nabu keyboard handling as he writes a BIOS to run his CP/M (re)port to Cloud CP/M to "netboot" via RS-422.

https://x.com/voyles_jason/status/1631865160607453184

1631929789689765890.a: @voyles_jason It is basically a Microsoft MSX system but like a year before that was a thing. You can add a single jumper to get the hardware very close. Then remap memory base address of certain things. Donkey Kong for ColecoVision can also be ported. I have a broken Colecovision to fix also.

1631930895421587458.a: @voyles_jason My plan to tackle the machine is to do a teardown and make sure all the hardware is working. I think I have a box of sketchy old Z80 system chips and 8k UV EPROMs to adjust firmware. Then look try to mirror the firmware's keyboard input handler and map from BT scan codes.

1631931523799629824.a:
@voyles_jason Once that works then add macro file to the interface. Grab a fancy BT keyboard with extra buttons. Map buttosn to macros to run on the Nabu. So you don't need to remember a bunch of the weird CP/M et al commands so much. Like a Gateway 2000 AnyKey:

1631933557034610691.a: @voyles_jason Well, assuming I can get any of these Sun keyboards to work. Type 6 was made mostly out of the wish not to go bankrupt. They tend to just start disintegrating. 1631937946474487808.a: @voyles_jason Oh, also, Nabu has joystalks or whatever. Not clear how to attack that yet but maybe just a mouse interface and an Atari joystick port somewhere.
